9941#[pymethods]
9942impl PySemanticTensorContentWitness {
9943    /// Enqueue verification against this witness's original content baseline.
9944    /// Native checks their original pointers, metadata and device bytes. DLPack
9945    /// callbacks run without Session, reader or task-state locks; their complete
9946    /// handoff must leave the task and admitted authority snapshot unchanged.
9947    ///
9948    /// Call after hooks and before the first dependent read. All preceding writes
9949    /// must be ordered on the declared stream, with no concurrent writes through
9950    /// the final dependent use. A byte mismatch fatally invalidates the CUDA
9951    /// context. Returning None means only that the guard was enqueued; the
9952    /// original cold observation must propagate any device error before accepting
9953    /// results. Do not reset or retry a failed task. No digest or status is copied
9954    /// to the host, and verification grants no replay or import authority.
9955    /// Workers may call this one method while the issuing Runtime retains the
9956    /// complete witness and original graph through guaranteed creator cleanup.
9957    /// Use the actual consumer stream or legacy default stream 1. Per-thread
9958    /// default stream 2 is rejected on every thread before producer handoff.
9959    #[pyo3(signature = (*, tensors, consumer_stream))]
9960    fn verify(
9961        &self,
9962        py: Python<'_>,
9963        tensors: &Bound<'_, PyAny>,
9964        consumer_stream: &Bound<'_, PyAny>,
9965    ) -> PyResult<()> {
9966        let session = self.session.borrow(py);
9967        let binding = {
9968            let owner = session.witness_owner()?;
9969            self.parent.binding(py, &owner, true)?
9970        };
9971        let mut budget = 16 * 1024 * 1024;
9972        let stream = parse_witness_consumer_stream(consumer_stream, &mut budget)?;
9973        let device = session.device_ordinal;
9974        let check = || -> PyResult<()> {
9975            let owner = session.witness_owner()?;
9976            if self.parent.binding(py, &owner, true)? != binding {
9977                return Err(invalid(
9978                    "tensor content authority changed during producer callback",
9979                ));
9980            }
9981            self.parent.check_producer_stream(py, &owner, stream)
9982        };
9983        check()?;
9984        let ParsedTensorInputs {
9985            handoff: tensors,
9986            producers: _producers,
9987        } = parse_tensor_inputs_guarded(tensors, &mut budget, device, stream, &check)?;
9988        let mut owner = session.witness_owner()?;
9989        match &self.parent {
9990            ContentStepOwner::Published(parent) => {
9991                let parent = parent.borrow(py);
9992                let task_use = parent.task_use.borrow(py);
9993                task_use.require_current(&owner)?;
9994                let state = task_use.state()?;
9995                let (operation, snapshot) = state.content_handoff_binding()?;
9996                if (Some(operation), snapshot) != binding {
9997                    return Err(invalid(
9998                        "tensor content authority changed during producer handoff",
9999                    ));
10000                }
10001                let lease = parent.lease()?;
10002                owner.retained_step_identity(&lease).map_err(xlog_err)?;
10003                owner
10004                    .verify_tensor_content(&lease, &self.inner, tensors.into_native(), stream)
10005                    .map_err(xlog_err)
10006            }
10007            ContentStepOwner::Prepared(step) => {
10008                let step = step.borrow(py);
10009                let task_use = step.task_use.borrow(py);
10010                task_use.require_identity(&owner)?;
10011                let state = task_use.state()?;
10012                if state.prepared_content_binding(&step.scope)? != binding {
10013                    return Err(invalid(
10014                        "tensor content authority changed during producer handoff",
10015                    ));
10016                }
10017                owner
10018                    .verify_prepared_tensor_content(
10019                        &step.inner,
10020                        &self.inner,
10021                        tensors.into_native(),
10022                        stream,
10023                    )
10024                    .map_err(xlog_err)
10025            }
10026        }
10027    }
10028}

10078    update: Option<Py<PySemanticPreparedStep>>,
10079    target: Option<SemanticPreparedStep>,
10080    completion: Option<RetainedTargetCompletion>,

10092
10093impl Drop for PySemanticRetainedReplayMember {
10094    fn drop(&mut self) {
10095        if self.completed.load(Ordering::Acquire) {
10096            return;
10097        }
10098        let _ = Python::try_attach(|py| {
10099            let session = self.session.borrow(py);
10100            if let Some(owner) = session
10101                .inner
10102                .lock()
10103                .unwrap_or_else(std::sync::PoisonError::into_inner)
10104                .as_mut()
10105            {
10106                owner.abort();
10107            }
10108            session.importing.store(false, Ordering::Release);
10109            if let Ok(mut state) = self.task_use.borrow(py).state() {
10110                state.phase = TaskUsePhase::Refused;
10111            }
10112        });
10113    }
10114}
10115
10116#[cfg(feature = "semantic-policy")]
10117#[pymethods]
10118impl PySemanticRetainedReplayMember {
10119    /// Record this original replay's single actor or edit contribution to the
10120    /// target Update graph. The original model output, published reader and
10121    /// tape stay owned by this handle through both mutually exclusive banks.
10122    #[pyo3(signature = (update_step, bank, *, consumer_stream))]
10123    fn group_update_vjp(
10124        &self,
10125        py: Python<'_>,
10126        update_step: Py<PySemanticPreparedStep>,
10127        bank: &Bound<'_, PyAny>,
10128        consumer_stream: &Bound<'_, PyAny>,
10129    ) -> PyResult<Py<PyTuple>> {
10130        let bank = usize::try_from(ColdValue::read(bank, &mut 128, 0)?.unsigned()?)
10131            .map_err(|_| invalid("group Update bank exceeds native address space"))?;
10132        if bank > 1 || self.completed.load(Ordering::Acquire) {
10133            return Err(invalid("retained replay has no open group Update bank"));
10134        }
10135        let stream = parse_witness_consumer_stream(consumer_stream, &mut 128)?;
10136        let source_session = self.session.borrow(py);
10137        source_session.require_creator()?;
10138        if !source_session.importing.load(Ordering::Acquire) {
10139            return Err(invalid(
10140                "original replay is no longer retained for group backward",
10141            ));
10142        }
10143        let update = update_step.borrow(py);
10144        if self.session.as_ptr() == update.session.as_ptr() {
10145            return Err(invalid(
10146                "historical group member requires a distinct target Session",
10147            ));
10148        }
10149        let target_session = update.session.borrow(py);
10150        target_session.require_creator()?;
10151        update.require_task(py, &update.task_use.borrow(py))?;
10152        let mut use_state = self
10153            .group_use
10154            .lock()
10155            .map_err(|_| PyRuntimeError::new_err("retained group use is poisoned"))?;
10156        let delivery = use_state.deliveries[bank]
10157            .as_ref()
10158            .ok_or_else(|| invalid("original group gradient delivery is absent"))?
10159            .borrow(py);
10160        if !delivery.activated_once.load(Ordering::Acquire)
10161            || delivery
10162                .handles
10163                .lock()
10164                .map_err(|_| PyRuntimeError::new_err("group gradient-delivery owner is poisoned"))?
10165                .is_none()
10166        {
10167            return Err(invalid(
10168                "original group gradient delivery must be active during this bank's VJP",
10169            ));
10170        }
10171        drop(delivery);
10172        if !use_state.gradient_banks[bank]
10173            || use_state.banks[bank]
10174            || use_state
10175                .target
10176                .as_ref()
10177                .is_some_and(|bound| !bound.same_handle(&update.inner))
10178        {
10179            return Err(invalid(
10180                "retained replay already served this bank or another Update",
10181            ));
10182        }
10183        let mut target_owner = target_session.owner()?;
10184        update.content_binding_with_owner(py, &target_owner)?;
10185        let mut source_owner = source_session.owner()?;
10186        let parent = self.parent.borrow(py);
10187        let lease = parent.lease()?;
10188        let invocation = self.invocation.borrow(py);
10189        let gradients = target_owner
10190            .record_imported_policy_group_vjp(
10191                &update.inner,
10192                bank,
10193                &mut source_owner,
10194                &lease,
10195                invocation.rng,
10196                self.replay_ordinal,
10197                &self.replay_row,
10198                stream,
10199            )
10200            .map_err(xlog_err)?;
10201        let capsules = gradients
10202            .into_dlpack()
10203            .map_err(xlog_err)?
10204            .into_iter()
10205            .map(|tensor| {
10206                let tensor = retain_export_owner(
10207                    tensor,
10208                    self.session.clone_ref(py),
10209                    source_session.owner_thread,
10210                )?;
10211                crate::dlpack_capsule_from_tensor(py, tensor)
10212            })
10213            .collect::<PyResult<Vec<_>>>()?;
10214        use_state.banks[bank] = true;
10215        if use_state.update.is_none() {
10216            use_state.update = Some(update_step.clone_ref(py));
10217        }
10218        if use_state.target.is_none() {
10219            use_state.target = Some(update.inner.clone());
10220        }
10221        Ok(PyTuple::new(py, capsules)?.unbind())
10222    }
10223
10224    /// Record completed execution of the published target Update. This does
10225    /// not release the source: its allocations remain alive until the target
10226    /// executable and all of its step owners have retired.
10227    fn confirm_published_target(&self, py: Python<'_>) -> PyResult<()> {
10228        self.confirm_target_completion(py, None)
10229    }
10230
10231    /// Record completed execution of a skipped or refused target Update.
10232    /// No group VJP is inferred from this terminal outcome.
10233    fn confirm_unpublished_target(
10234        &self,
10235        py: Python<'_>,
10236        update_step: Py<PySemanticPreparedStep>,
10237    ) -> PyResult<()> {
10238        self.confirm_target_completion(py, Some(update_step))
10239    }
10240
10241    /// Retire the retained original after target segment retirement. The
10242    /// normal import authority refresh and reader release still run once.
10243    fn finish(&self, py: Python<'_>) -> PyResult<()> {
10244        self.finish_retained_import(py, None)
10245    }
10246
10247    /// Retire a retained original after its nonpublishing target has retired.
10248    fn finish_without_published_update(
10249        &self,
10250        py: Python<'_>,
10251        update_step: Py<PySemanticPreparedStep>,
10252    ) -> PyResult<()> {
10253        self.finish_retained_import(py, Some(update_step))
10254    }
10255}

10257#[cfg(feature = "semantic-policy")]
10258impl PySemanticRetainedReplayMember {
10259    fn confirm_target_completion(
10260        &self,
10261        py: Python<'_>,
10262        unpublished_update: Option<Py<PySemanticPreparedStep>>,
10263    ) -> PyResult<()> {
10264        if self.completed.load(Ordering::Acquire) {
10265            return Err(invalid("retained replay member has already finished"));
10266        }
10267        let mut use_state = self
10268            .group_use
10269            .lock()
10270            .map_err(|_| PyRuntimeError::new_err("retained group use is poisoned"))?;
10271        if use_state.completion.is_some() {
10272            return Err(invalid(
10273                "retained target completion has already been confirmed",
10274            ));
10275        }
10276        let (update, completion) = if let Some(update) = unpublished_update {
10277            let changed_target = {
10278                let target = update.borrow(py);
10279                use_state
10280                    .target
10281                    .as_ref()
10282                    .is_some_and(|bound| !bound.same_handle(&target.inner))
10283            };
10284            if changed_target
10285                || use_state
10286                    .update
10287                    .as_ref()
10288                    .is_some_and(|bound| !bound.is(&update))
10289            {
10290                return Err(invalid(
10291                    "unpublished Update differs from the retained member's bound target",
10292                ));
10293            }
10294            (update, RetainedTargetCompletion::Unpublished)
10295        } else {
10296            if use_state.banks != [true, true] || use_state.gradient_banks != [true, true] {
10297                return Err(invalid("retained replay requires both Update banks and original physical gradient deliveries"));
10298            }
10299            (
10300                use_state
10301                    .update
10302                    .as_ref()
10303                    .ok_or_else(|| invalid("retained replay has no original Update owner"))?
10304                    .clone_ref(py),
10305                RetainedTargetCompletion::Published,
10306            )
10307        };
10308        for delivery in use_state.deliveries.iter().flatten() {
10309            let delivery = delivery.borrow(py);
10310            if delivery.activated_once.load(Ordering::Acquire)
10311                && delivery
10312                    .handles
10313                    .lock()
10314                    .map_err(|_| {
10315                        PyRuntimeError::new_err("group gradient-delivery owner is poisoned")
10316                    })?
10317                    .is_some()
10318            {
10319                return Err(invalid(
10320                    "retained gradient delivery is still active during target completion",
10321                ));
10322            }
10323        }
10324        {
10325            let update = update.borrow(py);
10326            let target_session = update.session.borrow(py);
10327            target_session.require_creator()?;
10328            let target_owner = target_session.owner()?;
10329            match completion {
10330                RetainedTargetCompletion::Published => target_owner
10331                    .require_recorded_group_critic(&update.inner)
10332                    .map_err(xlog_err)?,
10333                RetainedTargetCompletion::Unpublished => target_owner
10334                    .require_completed_unpublished_group_update(&update.inner)
10335                    .map_err(xlog_err)?,
10336            }
10337            use_state.target = Some(update.inner.clone());
10338        }
10339        use_state.update = Some(update);
10340        use_state.completion = Some(completion);
10341        Ok(())
10342    }
10343
10344    fn finish_retained_import(
10345        &self,
10346        py: Python<'_>,
10347        unpublished_update: Option<Py<PySemanticPreparedStep>>,
10348    ) -> PyResult<()> {
10349        if self.completed.load(Ordering::Acquire) {
10350            return Err(invalid("retained replay member has already finished"));
10351        }
10352        let update = {
10353            let use_state = self
10354                .group_use
10355                .lock()
10356                .map_err(|_| PyRuntimeError::new_err("retained group use is poisoned"))?;
10357            let expected_completion = if unpublished_update.is_some() {
10358                RetainedTargetCompletion::Unpublished
10359            } else {
10360                RetainedTargetCompletion::Published
10361            };
10362            if use_state.completion != Some(expected_completion) {
10363                return Err(invalid(
10364                    "retained target completion must be confirmed before source retirement",
10365                ));
10366            }
10367            let update = use_state
10368                .update
10369                .as_ref()
10370                .ok_or_else(|| invalid("retained replay has no original Update owner"))?;
10371            if unpublished_update
10372                .as_ref()
10373                .is_some_and(|given| !given.is(update))
10374            {
10375                return Err(invalid(
10376                    "unpublished Update differs from the confirmed target",
10377                ));
10378            }
10379            update.clone_ref(py)
10380        };
10381        {
10382            let update = update.borrow(py);
10383            let target_session = update.session.borrow(py);
10384            target_session.require_creator()?;
10385            let target_owner = target_session.owner()?;
10386            target_owner
10387                .require_retired_prepared_step(&update.inner)
10388                .map_err(xlog_err)?;
10389        }
10390        let session = self.session.borrow(py);
10391        session.require_creator()?;
10392        if !session.importing.load(Ordering::Acquire) {
10393            return Err(invalid("retained original import was already closed"));
10394        }
10395        let issued = self.task_use.borrow(py);
10396        let acquired = self.parent.borrow(py);
10397        let controller = PySemanticTransitionController {
10398            session: self.session.clone_ref(py),
10399            identity: Arc::clone(&self.controller_identity),
10400        };
10401        let mut import = ColdImportGuard {
10402            session: &session,
10403            issuance: issued.issuance.clone(),
10404            original_decisions: Some(Arc::clone(&self.original_decisions)),
10405            committed: false,
10406            deferred: false,
10407        };
10408        let completion = (|| -> PyResult<()> {
10409            let mut owner = session.owner()?;
10410            let state =
10411                controller.execution_state(py, &issued, &acquired, &owner, Some(&import))?;
10412            if PySemanticTransitionController::execution_binding(&state, true)? != self.expected {
10413                return Err(invalid(
10414                    "retained replay authority changed before original final use",
10415                ));
10416            }
10417            drop(state);
10418            let invocation = self.invocation.borrow(py);
10419            invocation.start_final_use()?;
10420            owner
10421                .finish_policy_invocation(&*acquired.lease()?, invocation.rng, 1)
10422                .map_err(xlog_err)
10423        })();
10424        let result = controller.finalize_replay_import(
10425            py,
10426            &self.task_use,
10427            &self.parent,
10428            &issued,
10429            &acquired,
10430            &self.material,
10431            self.finish_invocation.bind(py),
10432            self.refresh_snapshot.bind(py),
10433            &import,
10434            &self.expected,
10435            completion,
10436        );
10437        if result.is_ok() {
10438            import.committed = true;
10439            let mut use_state = self
10440                .group_use
10441                .lock()
10442                .unwrap_or_else(std::sync::PoisonError::into_inner);
10443            use_state.update = None;
10444            use_state.target = None;
10445            use_state.deliveries = std::array::from_fn(|_| None);
10446            self.completed.store(true, Ordering::Release);
10447        } else if let Ok(mut state) = issued.state() {
10448            state.phase = TaskUsePhase::Refused;
10449        }
10450        result
10451    }
10452}

10454#[cfg(feature = "semantic-policy")]
10455#[pymethods]
10456impl PySemanticPolicyInvocation {
10457    /// Original native coordinates, not a successor or caller-supplied seed.
10458    #[getter]
10459    fn rng(&self, py: Python<'_>) -> PyResult<(u32, u64, u8, u32)> {
10460        self.session.borrow(py).require_creator()?;
10461        self.require_public_result(py)?;
10462        Ok((
10463            self.rng.model_generation,
10464            self.rng.stream_serial,
10465            self.rng.family_id,
10466            self.rng.proposal,
10467        ))
10468    }
10469
10470    /// None for publication, otherwise a typed native refusal dictionary.
10471    /// Canary refusal dictionaries retain exact device-authored measurement,
10472    /// frozen-bound, resource and identity evidence.
10473    /// A refusal contains no published result or differentiable receipt bank.
10474    #[getter]
10475    fn refusal(&self, py: Python<'_>) -> PyResult<Option<Py<PyDict>>> {
10476        self.session.borrow(py).require_creator()?;
10477        self.require_public_result(py)?;
10478        transition_refusal_report(py, &self.outcome)
10479    }
10480
10481    /// Actual native evaluator output and full unclipped tuple weight.
10482    /// These cold results are not a differentiable surrogate selected-score.
10483    #[getter]
10484    fn result(&self, py: Python<'_>) -> PyResult<Py<PyDict>> {
10485        self.session.borrow(py).require_creator()?;
10486        self.require_public_result(py)?;
10487        let observation = self.published_observation()?;
10488        let task = observation
10489            .task_evaluation
10490            .as_ref()
10491            .ok_or_else(|| invalid("policy invocation has no native task evaluation"))?;
10492        let result = PyDict::new(py);
10493        result.set_item("binding", PyBytes::new(py, task.binding.as_bytes()))?;
10494        result.set_item("winner", task.winner)?;
10495        result.set_item("return_value", task.return_value)?;
10496        result.set_item("importance_weight", observation.importance_weight)?;
10497        result.set_item("next_proposal", observation.next_proposal)?;
10498        result.set_item("query_count", task.query_count)?;
10499        result.set_item(
10500            "truths",
10501            PyTuple::new(
10502                py,
10503                task.facts
10504                    .iter()
10505                    .map(|fact| (fact.truth[0], fact.truth[1], fact.truth[2])),
10506            )?,
10507        )?;
10508        result.set_item(
10509            "correct",
10510            PyTuple::new(
10511                py,
10512                task.facts
10513                    .iter()
10514                    .map(|fact| (fact.correct[0], fact.correct[1], fact.correct[2])),
10515            )?,
10516        )?;
10517        let program_rules = observation
10518            .lanes
10519            .iter()
10520            .map(|lane| {
10521                PyTuple::new(
10522                    py,
10523                    lane.program_rules.iter().map(|rule| {
10524                        rule.map(|rule| {
10525                            (
10526                                rule.head_predicate,
10527                                rule.left_predicate,
10528                                rule.right_predicate,
10529                                rule.body_count,
10530                                rule.head_variables[0],
10531                                rule.head_variables[1],
10532                                rule.left_variables[0],
10533                                rule.left_variables[1],
10534                                rule.right_variables[0],
10535                                rule.right_variables[1],
10536                            )
10537                        })
10538                    }),
10539                )
10540            })
10541            .collect::<PyResult<Vec<_>>>()?;
10542        result.set_item("program_rules", PyTuple::new(py, program_rules)?)?;
10543        result.set_item(
10544            "facts",
10545            PyTuple::new(
10546                py,
10547                task.facts.iter().map(|fact| {
10548                    (
10549                        (fact.correct[0], fact.correct[1]),
10550                        fact.g,
10551                        fact.p,
10552                        fact.c,
10553                        fact.v,
10554                        fact.eligible,
10555                    )
10556                }),
10557            )?,
10558        )?;
10559        Ok(result.unbind())
10560    }
10561
10562    /// Fresh copies of all 136 original receipts. Mutating these Python copies
10563    /// cannot replace the native receipt/support buffers used by backward.
10564    #[getter]
10565    fn receipts(&self, py: Python<'_>) -> PyResult<Py<PyTuple>> {
10566        self.session.borrow(py).require_creator()?;
10567        self.require_public_result(py)?;
10568        let receipts = self.published_observation()?.components.iter().map(|r| {
10569            let row = PyDict::new(py);
10570            macro_rules! scalar { ($($name:ident),+ $(,)?) => { $(row.set_item(stringify!($name), r.$name)?;)+ }; }
10571            scalar!(proposal, catalogue_generation, ordinal, lane, slot, field, kind, choice,
10572                legal_count, active_count, draw, cdf_start, cdf_end, mass, active_fields, null_fields);
10573            row.set_item("catalogue_digest", PyBytes::new(py, r.catalogue_digest.as_bytes()))?;
10574            row.set_item("admission_binding", PyBytes::new(py, r.admission_binding.as_bytes()))?;
10575            row.set_item("key", (r.key[0], r.key[1]))?;
10576            row.set_item("counter", (r.counter[0], r.counter[1], r.counter[2], r.counter[3]))?;
10577            row.set_item("random_words", (r.random_words[0], r.random_words[1], r.random_words[2], r.random_words[3]))?;
10578            row.set_item("p", (r.p[0], r.p[1], r.p[2]))?;
10579            row.set_item("q", (r.q[0], r.q[1], r.q[2]))?;
10580            row.set_item("factor_denominator", (r.factor_denominator[0], r.factor_denominator[1], r.factor_denominator[2]))?;
10581            Ok(row)
10582        }).collect::<PyResult<Vec<_>>>()?;
10583        Ok(PyTuple::new(py, receipts)?.unbind())
10584    }
10585
10586    /// Supply the original loss's contiguous FP64[136] selected-score
10587    /// cotangents. Returns FP32 parameter, full MASK and zero baseline adjoints,
10588    /// followed by their three full FP64 E[...,2] error envelopes and three
10589    /// contiguous FP64 D[2,...,4] bounds in actor/full and (M,O,U,I) order.
10590    /// Explicit external coefficients seed only full, not an actor source.
10591    /// Only the first three are autograd cotangents.
10592    /// They are applied to the retained original graph. No model
10593    /// getter, second forward, Python selected-score or new primal leaf is used.
10594    /// Adjoint consumers enqueue on ``consumer_stream`` after this returns;
10595    /// readiness is ordered by the native producer event without a host wait.
10596    /// Stream 1 names the legacy default; streams 0 and 2 are refused.
10597    /// This is a single-use handoff, including uncertain producer failures.
10598    #[pyo3(signature = (score_cotangents, *, consumer_stream))]
10599    fn backward(
10600        &self,
10601        py: Python<'_>,
10602        score_cotangents: &Bound<'_, PyAny>,
10603        consumer_stream: &Bound<'_, PyAny>,
10604    ) -> PyResult<Py<PyTuple>> {
10605        self.session.borrow(py).require_creator()?;
10606        self.require_public_result(py)?;
10607        let expected = {
10608            let session = self.session.borrow(py);
10609            let owner = session.owner()?;
10610            self.final_use_binding(py, &owner)?
10611        };
10612        if !self.training {
10613            return Err(invalid(
10614                "policy backward requires the original training use",
10615            ));
10616        }
10617        self.published_observation()?;
10618        let mut budget = 4096;
10619        let consumer_stream = parse_witness_consumer_stream(consumer_stream, &mut budget)?;
10620        let producer_stream = i64::try_from(consumer_stream)
10621            .map_err(|_| invalid("consumer stream exceeds the DLPack signed stream range"))?;
10622        self.start_final_use()?;
10623        let check = || {
10624            let session = self.session.borrow(py);
10625            let owner = session.owner()?;
10626            if self.final_use_binding(py, &owner)? != expected {
10627                return Err(invalid(
10628                    "policy backward authority changed during producer handoff",
10629                ));
10630            }
10631            Ok(())
10632        };
10633        validate_producer_device_guarded(
10634            score_cotangents,
10635            self.session.borrow(py).device_ordinal,
10636            &check,
10637        )?;
10638        let mut handoff = TensorHandoff(vec![crate::dlpack_from_py_for_stream_guarded(
10639            score_cotangents,
10640            producer_stream,
10641            &check,
10642        )?]);
10643        let session = self.session.borrow(py);
10644        let mut owner = session.owner()?;
10645        // A producer callback may have terminally aborted the shared owner.
10646        // Recheck the actual original parent and exact authority before
10647        // relinquishing the quarantined handoff or launching the native VJP.
10648        if self.final_use_binding(py, &owner)? != expected {
10649            return Err(invalid(
10650                "policy backward authority changed during producer handoff",
10651            ));
10652        }
10653        let tensor = handoff.0.pop().expect("one original cotangent producer");
10654        let gradients = match &self._parent {
10655            ContentStepOwner::Published(_) => {
10656                owner.backward_policy_dlpack(self.rng, tensor, consumer_stream)
10657            }
10658            ContentStepOwner::Prepared(step) => owner.backward_prepared_policy_dlpack(
10659                &step.borrow(py).inner,
10660                self.rng,
10661                tensor,
10662                consumer_stream,
10663            ),
10664        }
10665        .map_err(xlog_err)?;
10666        // The actual parent also owns the original continuation producers and
10667        // Session. All capsule owners preserve them through late consumers,
10668        // with final Python decrefs deferred to the creating thread.
10669        let export_owner = || -> PublishedExportOwner {
10670            match &self._parent {
10671                ContentStepOwner::Published(parent) => parent.clone_ref(py).into(),
10672                ContentStepOwner::Prepared(step) => step.clone_ref(py).into(),
10673            }
10674        };
10675        let capsules = gradients
10676            .into_dlpack()
10677            .map_err(xlog_err)?
10678            .into_iter()
10679            .map(|tensor| {
10680                let tensor = retain_export_owner(tensor, export_owner(), session.owner_thread)?;
10681                crate::dlpack_capsule_from_tensor(py, tensor)
10682            })
10683            .collect::<PyResult<Vec<_>>>()?;
10684        Ok(PyTuple::new(py, capsules)?.unbind())
10685    }
10686
10687    /// Consume this prepared proposal's exact retained tape against the
10688    /// prepared Update step's resident actor/critic/cost objective. The caller
10689    /// invokes this method for every proposal invocation in the frozen segment
10690    /// and joins every returned root into one GraphTask. Native selection makes
10691    /// unselected invocations graph-connected zeros; Python never reads the
10692    /// selected ordinal, reconstructs selected scores, or runs a second primal.
10693    ///
10694    /// Returns FP32 parameter, full MASK and component-baseline adjoints,
10695    /// then their three full FP64 E[...,2] ordinary/underflow envelopes and
10696    /// three contiguous FP64 D[2,...,4] bounds in actor/full and (M,O,U,I)
10697    /// order. E and D.full.O/U come from the same coherent result. These are
10698    /// selected-tape bounds, not pre-draw support/prefix coverage. Only the first three
10699    /// capsules are autograd cotangents. This is a single-use handoff, including
10700    /// uncertain native failures.
10701    #[pyo3(signature = (update_step, *, consumer_stream))]
10702    fn backward_selected(
10703        &self,
10704        py: Python<'_>,
10705        update_step: Py<PySemanticPreparedStep>,
10706        consumer_stream: &Bound<'_, PyAny>,
10707    ) -> PyResult<Py<PyTuple>> {
10708        self.session.borrow(py).require_creator()?;
10709        self.require_public_result(py)?;
10710        let policy_step = match &self._parent {
10711            ContentStepOwner::Prepared(step) => step,
10712            ContentStepOwner::Published(_) => {
10713                return Err(invalid(
10714                    "device-selected policy backward requires an original prepared proposal",
10715                ));
10716            }
10717        };
10718        let expected = {
10719            let session = self.session.borrow(py);
10720            let owner = session.owner()?;
10721            self.final_use_binding(py, &owner)?
10722        };
10723        if !self.training {
10724            return Err(invalid(
10725                "device-selected policy backward requires the original training use",
10726            ));
10727        }
10728        self.published_observation()?;
10729        let mut budget = 4096;
10730        let consumer_stream = parse_witness_consumer_stream(consumer_stream, &mut budget)?;
10731        {
10732            let update = update_step.borrow(py);
10733            if self.session.as_ptr() != update.session.as_ptr() {
10734                return Err(invalid(
10735                    "device-selected policy backward requires an Update from the same Session",
10736                ));
10737            }
10738            let task_use = self._task_use.borrow(py);
10739            update.require_task(py, &task_use)?;
10740        }
10741        self.start_final_use()?;
10742        let session = self.session.borrow(py);
10743        let mut owner = session.owner()?;
10744        if self.final_use_binding(py, &owner)? != expected {
10745            return Err(invalid(
10746                "policy backward authority changed before resident objective use",
10747            ));
10748        }
10749        let gradients = owner
10750            .backward_selected_prepared_policy(
10751                &policy_step.borrow(py).inner,
10752                &update_step.borrow(py).inner,
10753                self.rng,
10754                consumer_stream,
10755            )
10756            .map_err(xlog_err)?;
10757        let export_owner = || policy_step.clone_ref(py);
10758        let capsules = gradients
10759            .into_dlpack()
10760            .map_err(xlog_err)?
10761            .into_iter()
10762            .map(|tensor| {
10763                let tensor = retain_export_owner(tensor, export_owner(), session.owner_thread)?;
10764                crate::dlpack_capsule_from_tensor(py, tensor)
10765            })
10766            .collect::<PyResult<Vec<_>>>()?;
10767        Ok(PyTuple::new(py, capsules)?.unbind())
10768    }
10769
10770    /// Finish the original published or refused inference use after consumers are enqueued.
10771    ///
10772    /// ``consumer_stream`` must be the explicit CUDA stream containing those
10773    /// consumers (legacy default stream 1 is allowed; 0 and 2 are not). Native
10774    /// finalization joins that stream without a host wait and retires only this
10775    /// invocation's retained policy tape. It does not release the parent.
10776    /// Published training invocations require ``backward`` or, after a completed
10777    /// group Update, ``finish_recorded_training`` for a consumed tape or
10778    /// ``finish_unselected_recorded_training`` for an unselected tape. Refused
10779    /// training invocations require ``finish_refusal``. Final use is one-shot,
10780    /// including uncertain native failures.
10781    #[pyo3(signature = (*, consumer_stream))]
10782    fn finish_inference(&self, py: Python<'_>, consumer_stream: &Bound<'_, PyAny>) -> PyResult<()> {
10783        self.session.borrow(py).require_creator()?;
10784        self.require_public_result(py)?;
10785        if self.training {
10786            return Err(invalid(
10787                "policy inference completion requires the original inference use",
10788            ));
10789        }
10790        self.finish_final_use(py, consumer_stream)
10791    }
10792
10793    /// Finish a published training invocation after its policy tape was already
10794    /// consumed by ``SemanticPreparedStep.temporal_update_vjp`` inside both
10795    /// branches of the exact prepared Update. This is a terminal ownership
10796    /// handoff only; it does not execute a second backward or policy VJP.
10797    ///
10798    /// Enqueue every final GraphTask/optimizer consumer on ``consumer_stream``
10799    /// before this call. Native validation binds the Proposal, Update and
10800    /// invocation to the same completed segment and exact recording identities.
10801    #[pyo3(signature = (update_step, *, consumer_stream))]
10802    fn finish_recorded_training(
10803        &self,
10804        py: Python<'_>,
10805        update_step: Py<PySemanticPreparedStep>,
10806        consumer_stream: &Bound<'_, PyAny>,
10807    ) -> PyResult<()> {
10808        self.finish_recorded_training_use(py, update_step, consumer_stream, false)
10809    }
10810
10811    /// Finish a published local Proposal that was outside the exact frozen
10812    /// actor/edit group. A completed, published Update must have recorded both
10813    /// full-group critic reductions; a completed Update that did not publish
10814    /// also permits terminal use without claiming a policy VJP. This tape must
10815    /// have no Update VJP. No synthetic gradient or second backward is produced.
10816    #[pyo3(signature = (update_step, *, consumer_stream))]
10817    fn finish_unselected_recorded_training(
10818        &self,
10819        py: Python<'_>,
10820        update_step: Py<PySemanticPreparedStep>,
10821        consumer_stream: &Bound<'_, PyAny>,
10822    ) -> PyResult<()> {
10823        self.finish_recorded_training_use(py, update_step, consumer_stream, true)
10824    }
10825
10826    /// Finish an actual native refusal from inference or training without a VJP.
10827    ///
10828    /// Enqueue final consumers on the explicit ``consumer_stream`` first.
10829    /// Stream 1 is allowed; 0 and 2 are refused. Published outcomes are not
10830    /// admitted here. This shares the one-shot final-use owner with ``backward``,
10831    /// ``finish_recorded_training`` and ``finish_inference`` and retains the
10832    /// parent for its later release.
10833    #[pyo3(signature = (*, consumer_stream))]
10834    fn finish_refusal(&self, py: Python<'_>, consumer_stream: &Bound<'_, PyAny>) -> PyResult<()> {
10835        self.session.borrow(py).require_creator()?;
10836        self.require_public_result(py)?;
10837        if !matches!(
10838            &self.outcome,
10839            xlog_cuda::SemanticTransitionOutcome::Refused(_)
10840        ) {
10841            return Err(invalid(
10842                "policy refusal completion requires an actual native refusal",
10843            ));
10844        }
10845        self.finish_final_use(py, consumer_stream)
10846    }
10847}
10848
10849#[cfg(feature = "semantic-policy")]
10850impl PySemanticPolicyInvocation {
10851    fn finish_recorded_training_use(
10852        &self,
10853        py: Python<'_>,
10854        update_step: Py<PySemanticPreparedStep>,
10855        consumer_stream: &Bound<'_, PyAny>,
10856        unselected: bool,
10857    ) -> PyResult<()> {
10858        self.session.borrow(py).require_creator()?;
10859        self.require_public_result(py)?;
10860        if !self.training {
10861            return Err(invalid(
10862                "recorded training completion requires the original training use",
10863            ));
10864        }
10865        self.published_observation()?;
10866        let policy_step = match &self._parent {
10867            ContentStepOwner::Prepared(step) => step,
10868            ContentStepOwner::Published(_) => {
10869                return Err(invalid(
10870                    "recorded training completion requires an original prepared Proposal",
10871                ));
10872            }
10873        };
10874        {
10875            let update = update_step.borrow(py);
10876            if self.session.as_ptr() != update.session.as_ptr() {
10877                return Err(invalid(
10878                    "recorded training completion requires an Update from the same Session",
10879                ));
10880            }
10881            let task_use = self._task_use.borrow(py);
10882            update.require_task(py, &task_use)?;
10883        }
10884        let expected = {
10885            let session = self.session.borrow(py);
10886            let owner = session.owner()?;
10887            self.final_use_binding(py, &owner)?
10888        };
10889        let mut budget = 4096;
10890        let consumer_stream = parse_witness_consumer_stream(consumer_stream, &mut budget)?;
10891        self.start_final_use()?;
10892        let session = self.session.borrow(py);
10893        let mut owner = session.owner()?;
10894        if self.final_use_binding(py, &owner)? != expected {
10895            return Err(invalid(
10896                "policy authority changed before recorded training completion",
10897            ));
10898        }
10899        let result = if unselected {
10900            owner.finish_unselected_recorded_training_policy_invocation(
10901                &policy_step.borrow(py).inner,
10902                &update_step.borrow(py).inner,
10903                self.rng,
10904                consumer_stream,
10905            )
10906        } else {
10907            owner.finish_recorded_training_policy_invocation(
10908                &policy_step.borrow(py).inner,
10909                &update_step.borrow(py).inner,
10910                self.rng,
10911                consumer_stream,
10912            )
10913        };
10914        result.map_err(xlog_err)
10915    }
10916    fn finish_final_use(&self, py: Python<'_>, consumer_stream: &Bound<'_, PyAny>) -> PyResult<()> {
10917        let expected = {
10918            let session = self.session.borrow(py);
10919            let owner = session.owner()?;
10920            self.final_use_binding(py, &owner)?
10921        };
10922        let mut budget = 4096;
10923        let consumer_stream = parse_witness_consumer_stream(consumer_stream, &mut budget)?;
10924        self.start_final_use()?;
10925        let session = self.session.borrow(py);
10926        let mut owner = session.owner()?;
10927        if self.final_use_binding(py, &owner)? != expected {
10928            return Err(invalid("policy authority changed before final use"));
10929        }
10930        match &self._parent {
10931            ContentStepOwner::Published(parent) => {
10932                let parent = parent.borrow(py);
10933                let lease = parent.lease()?;
10934                owner.finish_policy_invocation(&lease, self.rng, consumer_stream)
10935            }
10936            ContentStepOwner::Prepared(step) => owner.finish_prepared_policy_invocation(
10937                &step.borrow(py).inner,
10938                self.rng,
10939                consumer_stream,
10940            ),
10941        }
10942        .map_err(xlog_err)
10943    }
10944
10945    fn published_observation(&self) -> PyResult<&xlog_cuda::SemanticTransitionObservation> {
10946        match &self.outcome {
10947            xlog_cuda::SemanticTransitionOutcome::Published(observation) => Ok(observation),
10948            xlog_cuda::SemanticTransitionOutcome::Refused(_) => Err(invalid(
10949                "refused policy invocation has no published result or differentiable receipts",
10950            )),
10951        }
10952    }
10953
10954    fn final_use_binding(
10955        &self,
10956        py: Python<'_>,
10957        owner: &SemanticTransitionSession,
10958    ) -> PyResult<(String, Vec<u8>)> {
10959        let task_use = self._task_use.borrow(py);
10960        if self.session.as_ptr() != task_use.session.as_ptr() {
10961            return Err(invalid(
10962                "policy final use belongs to another native Session",
10963            ));
10964        }
10965        let binding = match &self._parent {
10966            ContentStepOwner::Published(parent) => {
10967                let parent = parent.borrow(py);
10968                if self.session.as_ptr() != parent.session.as_ptr() {
10969                    return Err(invalid(
10970                        "policy final use belongs to another native Session",
10971                    ));
10972                }
10973                parent.require_task(py, &task_use)?;
10974                task_use.require_current(owner)?;
10975                owner
10976                    .retained_step_identity(&*parent.lease()?)
10977                    .map_err(xlog_err)?;
10978                let state = task_use.state()?;
10979                state.require_public_use()?;
10980                state.content_handoff_binding()?
10981            }
10982            ContentStepOwner::Prepared(step) => {
10983                let step = step.borrow(py);
10984                if self.session.as_ptr() != step.session.as_ptr() {
10985                    return Err(invalid(
10986                        "policy final use belongs to another native Session",
10987                    ));
10988                }
10989                step.require_task(py, &task_use)?;
10990                task_use.require_identity(owner)?;
10991                owner.prepared_stream(&step.inner).map_err(xlog_err)?;
10992                let state = task_use.state()?;
10993                state.require_public_use()?;
10994                let (operation, snapshot) = state.prepared_content_binding(&step.scope)?;
10995                (
10996                    operation.ok_or_else(|| {
10997                        invalid("policy final use requires actual admitted execution")
10998                    })?,
10999                    snapshot,
11000                )
11001            }
11002        };
11003        let operation = if self.training {
11004            "training"
11005        } else {
11006            "inference"
11007        };
11008        if binding.0 != operation {
11009            return Err(invalid(
11010                "policy final use requires the original admitted operation",
11011            ));
11012        }
11013        Ok(binding)
11014    }
11015
11016    fn start_final_use(&self) -> PyResult<()> {
11017        let mut started = self
11018            .final_use_started
11019            .lock()
11020            .map_err(|_| invalid("policy final-use owner is poisoned"))?;
11021        if *started {
11022            return Err(invalid("policy final use has already started"));
11023        }
11024        *started = true;
11025        Ok(())
11026    }
11027
11028    fn require_public_result(&self, py: Python<'_>) -> PyResult<()> {
11029        let session = self.session.borrow(py);
11030        let owner = session.owner()?;
11031        if matches!(&self._parent, ContentStepOwner::Prepared(_)) {
11032            return self.final_use_binding(py, &owner).map(|_| ());
11033        }
11034        let task_use = self._task_use.borrow(py);
11035        task_use.require_current(&owner)?;
11036        let result = task_use.state()?.require_public_use();
11037        result
11038    }
11039}

11041fn descriptor_meaning_object(
11042    py: Python<'_>,
11043    descriptor: &xlog_cuda::SemanticActionDescriptor,
11044) -> PyResult<Py<PyAny>> {
11045    use xlog_cuda::SemanticActionDescriptor;
11046    let value = match descriptor {
11047        SemanticActionDescriptor::Target { predicate } => {
11048            ("target", predicate.0).into_pyobject(py)?.into_any()
11049        }
11050        SemanticActionDescriptor::Operand {
11051            scalar_type,
11052            sort_label,
11053            encoded_value,
11054        } => (
11055            "operand",
11056            scalar_type.to_code(),
11057            sort_label.as_str(),
11058            PyBytes::new(py, encoded_value),
11059        )
11060            .into_pyobject(py)?
11061            .into_any(),
11062        SemanticActionDescriptor::QualifierBundle { records } => (
11063            "qualifier_bundle",
11064            PyTuple::new(py, records.iter().copied())?,
11065        )
11066            .into_pyobject(py)?
11067            .into_any(),
11068        SemanticActionDescriptor::SupportEvent { source_record } => {
11069            ("support_event", *source_record)
11070                .into_pyobject(py)?
11071                .into_any()
11072        }
11073        SemanticActionDescriptor::RulePredicate { predicate } => {
11074            ("rule_predicate", *predicate).into_pyobject(py)?.into_any()
11075        }
11076        SemanticActionDescriptor::RuleVariable { index } => {
11077            ("rule_variable", *index).into_pyobject(py)?.into_any()
11078        }
11079    };
11080    Ok(value.unbind())
11081}

11083fn dependency_lineage_object(py: Python<'_>, dependencies: &[Dependency]) -> PyResult<Py<PyTuple>> {
11084    let rows = dependencies
11085        .iter()
11086        .map(|dependency| {
11087            (
11088                dependency.identity.as_str(),
11089                dependency.kind.as_str(),
11090                PyTuple::new(py, &dependency.data_parents)?,
11091                PyTuple::new(py, &dependency.control_parents)?,
11092                PyTuple::new(py, &dependency.live_envelopes)?,
11093                dependency.target,
11094                dependency
11095                    .native_record
11096                    .as_ref()
11097                    .map(|(kind, index)| (kind.as_str(), *index)),
11098            )
11099                .into_pyobject(py)
11100                .map(Bound::unbind)
11101        })
11102        .collect::<PyResult<Vec<_>>>()?;
11103    Ok(PyTuple::new(py, rows)?.unbind())
11104}
11105
11106fn release_python_producers(producers: &Mutex<Vec<Py<PyAny>>>) {
11107    let producers = std::mem::take(
11108        &mut *producers
11109            .lock()
11110            .unwrap_or_else(std::sync::PoisonError::into_inner),
11111    );
11112    drop(producers);
11113}

11115impl PySemanticPublishedParent {
11116    fn lease(&self) -> PyResult<MutexGuard<'_, SemanticPublishedLease>> {
11117        self.inner
11118            .lock()
11119            .map_err(|_| PyRuntimeError::new_err("published parent lease mutex is poisoned"))
11120    }
11121
11122    // The native reader has already joined its consumers and released. Drop
11123    // original autograd owners only after releasing every native/state lock:
11124    // their Python finalizers may call the controller again.
11125    fn release_continuation_producers(&self) {
11126        release_python_producers(&self.continuation_producers);
11127    }
11128
11129    fn require_task(&self, py: Python<'_>, task_use: &PySemanticTransitionTaskUse) -> PyResult<()> {
11130        let issued = self.task_use.borrow(py);
11131        issued.issuance.require_current()?;
11132        if !Arc::ptr_eq(&issued.controller, &task_use.controller)
11133            || !issued.issuance.same_as(&task_use.issuance)
11134            || issued.task_epoch != task_use.task_epoch
11135            || issued.task_identity != task_use.task_identity
11136        {
11137            return Err(invalid("published parent belongs to another task use"));
11138        }
11139        Ok(())
11140    }
11141
11142    fn content_binding_with_owner(
11143        &self,
11144        py: Python<'_>,
11145        owner: &SemanticTransitionSession,
11146    ) -> PyResult<(String, Vec<u8>)> {
11147        let task_use = self.task_use.borrow(py);
11148        task_use.require_current(owner)?;
11149        owner
11150            .published_identity(&*self.lease()?)
11151            .map_err(xlog_err)?;
11152        let binding = task_use.state()?.content_handoff_binding()?;
11153        Ok(binding)
11154    }
11155
11156    fn retained_content_binding_with_owner(
11157        &self,
11158        py: Python<'_>,
11159        owner: &SemanticTransitionSession,
11160    ) -> PyResult<(String, Vec<u8>)> {
11161        let task_use = self.task_use.borrow(py);
11162        task_use.require_current(owner)?;
11163        owner
11164            .retained_step_identity(&*self.lease()?)
11165            .map_err(xlog_err)?;
11166        let binding = task_use.state()?.content_handoff_binding()?;
11167        Ok(binding)
11168    }
11169
11170    fn release_native_ownership(
11171        &self,
11172        py: Python<'_>,
11173        consumer_streams: &Bound<'_, PyAny>,
11174        reader_only: bool,
11175    ) -> PyResult<()> {
11176        self.session.borrow(py).require_creator()?;
11177        let session = self.session.borrow(py);
11178        if session.importing.load(Ordering::Acquire) {
11179            return Err(invalid(
11180                "public parent release cannot interrupt a native import",
11181            ));
11182        }
11183        let mut budget = 4096;
11184        let streams = ColdValue::read(consumer_streams, &mut budget, 0)?;
11185        let streams = streams
11186            .sequence()?
11187            .iter()
11188            .map(ColdValue::unsigned)
11189            .collect::<PyResult<Vec<_>>>()?;
11190        let mut owner = session.owner()?;
11191        if session.importing.load(Ordering::Acquire) {
11192            return Err(invalid(
11193                "public parent release cannot interrupt a native import",
11194            ));
11195        }
11196        // Cleanup uses the opaque original lease, not a new use grant. Bank
11197        // retirement preserves Python producers and their original graph until
11198        // native final release confirms all late consumers have completed.
11199        if reader_only {
11200            owner
11201                .release_published_reader(&mut *self.lease()?, &streams)
11202                .map_err(xlog_err)?;
11203        } else {
11204            owner
11205                .release(&mut *self.lease()?, &streams)
11206                .map_err(xlog_err)?;
11207        }
11208        drop(owner);
11209        drop(session);
11210        if !reader_only {
11211            self.release_continuation_producers();
11212        }
11213        Ok(())
11214    }
11215}

11217#[pymethods]
11218impl PySemanticPublishedParent {
11219    /// Enqueue fatal device guards for the original sealed native ranges.
11220    /// ``ranges`` is an exact tuple/list of exact ``(role, index)`` rows. Role 1
11221    /// checks the original raw prefix range. Arbitrary aliases outside these
11222    /// ranges are not attested. Use the same acquired parent throughout.
11223    ///
11224    /// Call after hooks and before the first dependent read, ordering all prior
11225    /// writes on ``consumer_stream`` and preventing concurrent writes through
11226    /// final use. The Session joins the named stream, guards the sealed bytes,
11227    /// then joins guard completion back to the consumer without a host copy or
11228    /// synchronization. A mismatch fatally invalidates the CUDA context; returning
11229    /// None only means enqueue succeeded. The original cold observation must
11230    /// propagate failure before accepting results. Never reset or retry that task.
11231    #[pyo3(signature = (*, ranges, consumer_stream))]
11232    fn guard_content(
11233        &self,
11234        py: Python<'_>,
11235        ranges: &Bound<'_, PyAny>,
11236        consumer_stream: &Bound<'_, PyAny>,
11237    ) -> PyResult<()> {
11238        self.session.borrow(py).require_creator()?;
11239        let mut budget = 16 * 1024 * 1024;
11240        let ranges = parse_content_ranges(&ColdValue::read(ranges, &mut budget, 0)?)?;
11241        let stream = ColdValue::read(consumer_stream, &mut budget, 0)?.unsigned()?;
11242        let session = self.session.borrow(py);
11243        let mut owner = session.owner()?;
11244        let task_use = self.task_use.borrow(py);
11245        task_use.require_current(&owner)?;
11246        let state = task_use.state()?;
11247        state.content_handoff_binding()?;
11248        owner
11249            .guard_published_content(&*self.lease()?, &ranges, stream)
11250            .map_err(xlog_err)
11251    }
11252
11253    /// The sealed identity returned by this lease's single native Acquire.
11254    fn identity(&self, py: Python<'_>) -> PyResult<Py<PyTuple>> {
11255        self.session.borrow(py).require_creator()?;
11256        let session = self.session.borrow(py);
11257        let owner = session.owner()?;
11258        self.task_use.borrow(py).require_current(&owner)?;
11259        let identity = owner
11260            .published_identity(&*self.lease()?)
11261            .map_err(xlog_err)?;
11262        Ok((
11263            PyBytes::new(py, identity.instance.as_bytes()),
11264            identity.word,
11265            PyBytes::new(py, identity.logical_digest.as_bytes()),
11266            PyBytes::new(py, identity.state_digest.as_bytes()),
11267        )
11268            .into_pyobject(py)?
11269            .unbind())
11270    }

11272    /// Return the complete accepted ``(role, index)`` roster as an immutable

11276    /// Actual access through tensor(), record() or prefix() still checks content
11277    /// readiness. This roster grants no new use, import or replay authority.
11278    fn range_keys(&self, py: Python<'_>) -> PyResult<Py<PyTuple>> {

11292
11293    /// Project model metadata from this exact acquired parent. Returns:
11294    /// (parent_identity, descriptor_digest, semantic_root, prefix, ring,
11295    /// generations, contracts, capacities, numerical_state).
11296    ///
11297    /// ``semantic_root`` is (owner, slot, generation, digest, extents), with
11298    /// statement/support/version extents. It identifies the acquired XLOG root;
11299    /// it is not the parent state digest or the action catalogue binding.
11300    /// ``prefix`` contains CUDA DLPack capsules (U8[32] identity, U64[1] extent).
11301    /// ``ring`` contains capsules (U64[1] head, U64[32,8] original source slots).
11302    /// They view this acquired bank without copying, sorting or rotating rows.
11303    /// ``generations`` is (model, neural_bank, neural, cache, authority).
11304    /// ``contracts`` is (topology_identity, position_table_identity).
11305    /// ``capacities`` is (prefix, feedback, exclusive_position_bound).
11306    /// ``numerical_state`` is (model_geometry_digest, model_numerical_digest),

11312    /// instance/word; it is not the action catalogue's descriptor identity.

11314    /// The retained parent remains the owner: matching these values does not
11315    /// authenticate unrelated model inputs or issue a new use permission. Device

11318    #[pyo3(signature = (*, consumer_stream))]
11319    fn model_context(
11320        &self,
11321        py: Python<'_>,
11322        consumer_stream: &Bound<'_, PyAny>,
11323    ) -> PyResult<Py<PyTuple>> {

11336            crate::dlpack_capsule_from_tensor(

11338                retain_export_owner(tensor, self.session.clone_ref(py), session.owner_thread)?,
11339            )

11342            (
11343                PyBytes::new(py, parent.instance.as_bytes()),

11345                PyBytes::new(py, parent.logical_digest.as_bytes()),

11350                root.0,
11351                root.1,

11373    /// Export the exact selected resident neural bank without a device copy.
11374    /// Returns (parent_identity, generations, numerical_state, allocations,
11375    /// storages, views). Each allocation row is (native_provenance, U8 DLPack)

11377    /// span_bytes). View rows are (role, index, storage, byte_offset, layout),
11378    /// where layout preserves element size, scalar type, rank, logical axis,
11379    /// four dimensions and four byte strides.
11380    ///
11381    /// These aliases are read-only views of the actually selected bank, not the
11382    /// private late-backward copies returned by tensor_allocation(). Retain the
11383    /// parent and all framework aliases through final use, then release with all
11384    /// consumer streams. The retained reader prevents native bank reuse; matching
11385    /// metadata alone grants no authority and must not be rebound to other bytes.
11386    #[pyo3(signature = (*, consumer_stream))]
11387    fn resident_model_memory(
11388        &self,
11389        py: Python<'_>,
11390        consumer_stream: &Bound<'_, PyAny>,
11391    ) -> PyResult<Py<PyTuple>> {
11392        self.session.borrow(py).require_creator()?;
11393        let stream = ColdValue::read(consumer_stream, &mut 128, 0)?.unsigned()?;
11394        let session = self.session.borrow(py);

11396        self.task_use.borrow(py).require_current(&owner)?;
11397        let memory = owner
11398            .published_resident_model_memory(&*self.lease()?, stream)
11399            .map_err(xlog_err)?;

11401        let mut allocations = Vec::with_capacity(memory.allocations.len());
11402        for (provenance, tensor) in memory.allocations {

11404                retain_export_owner(tensor, self.session.clone_ref(py), session.owner_thread)?;
11405            allocations.push(
11406                (
11407                    Py::new(py, PyNativeTensorAllocation { provenance })?,
11408                    crate::dlpack_capsule_from_tensor(py, tensor)?,
11409                )
11410                    .into_pyobject(py)?

11413        }
11414        let storages = PyTuple::new(
11415            py,
11416            memory
11417                .storages
11418                .into_iter()
11419                .map(|storage| (storage.allocation, storage.byte_offset, storage.span_bytes)),
11420        )?;
11421        let views = PyTuple::new(
11422            py,
11423            memory.views.into_iter().map(|(view, layout)| {
11424                (
11425                    view.role,
11426                    view.index,
11427                    view.storage,
11428                    view.byte_offset,
11429                    (
11430                        layout.element_bytes,
11431                        layout.scalar_type,
11432                        layout.rank,
11433                        layout.logical_axis,
11434                        (
11435                            layout.dimensions[0],
11436                            layout.dimensions[1],
11437                            layout.dimensions[2],
11438                            layout.dimensions[3],
11439                        ),
11440                        (
11441                            layout.strides_bytes[0],
11442                            layout.strides_bytes[1],
11443                            layout.strides_bytes[2],
11444                            layout.strides_bytes[3],
11445                        ),
11446                    ),
11447                )
11448            }),
11449        )?;
11450        Ok((
11451            (
11452                PyBytes::new(py, parent.instance.as_bytes()),
11453                parent.word,
11454                PyBytes::new(py, parent.logical_digest.as_bytes()),
11455                PyBytes::new(py, parent.state_digest.as_bytes()),
11456            ),
11457            memory.generations,
11458            (
11459                PyBytes::new(py, memory.numerical_state.0.as_bytes()),
11460                PyBytes::new(py, memory.numerical_state.1.as_bytes()),
11461            ),
11462            PyTuple::new(py, allocations)?,
11463            storages,
11464            views,
11465        )
11466            .into_pyobject(py)?
11467            .unbind())
11468    }

11470    /// Resolve one descriptor in this live parent's native catalogue.
11471    ///
11472    /// Returns ((catalogue_generation, digest), meaning). Descriptor fields are
11473    /// 2 (target), 3..6 (operand), 11 (qualifier bundle), and 17 (support event).
11474    /// Category zero in these fields is NULL, represented by None; an empty
11475    /// qualifier bundle remains ("qualifier_bundle", ()). Operands retain the
11476    /// native scalar type code, sort label and exact encoded bytes. A support
11477    /// event refers to the admission's support array, not its statement array.
11478    ///
11479    /// This read-only projection grants no use authority and does not establish
11480    /// the causal origin of a model operand from equality of its bytes.
11481    fn descriptor_meaning(
11482        &self,
11483        py: Python<'_>,
11484        field: &Bound<'_, PyAny>,
11485        category: &Bound<'_, PyAny>,
11486    ) -> PyResult<Py<PyTuple>> {
11487        self.session.borrow(py).require_creator()?;
11488        if !field.is_exact_instance_of::<pyo3::types::PyInt>()
11489            || !category.is_exact_instance_of::<pyo3::types::PyInt>()
11490        {
11491            return Err(invalid("descriptor coordinates must be exact integers"));
11492        }
11493        let field = field.extract::<u32>()?;
11494        let category = category.extract::<u32>()?;
11495        if !matches!(field, 2 | 3..=6 | 11 | 17) {
11496            return Err(invalid("field does not contain descriptor categories"));
11497        }
11498        let session = self.session.borrow(py);
11499        let owner = session.owner()?;
11500        self.task_use.borrow(py).require_current(&owner)?;
11501        owner
11502            .published_identity(&*self.lease()?)
11503            .map_err(xlog_err)?;
11504        let cardinality = owner
11505            .components()
11506            .iter()
11507            .find(|entry| entry.field == field)
11508            .ok_or_else(|| invalid("descriptor field is absent from the native catalogue"))?
11509            .cardinality;
11510        if category >= cardinality {
11511            return Err(invalid("descriptor category exceeds the native catalogue"));
11512        }
11513        let meaning = if category == 0 {
11514            py.None()
11515        } else {
11516            descriptor_meaning_object(
11517                py,
11518                owner
11519                    .descriptor_meaning(field, category)
11520                    .ok_or_else(|| invalid("native descriptor category has no meaning"))?,
11521            )?
11522        };
11523        let binding = owner.binding();
11524        Ok((
11525            (
11526                binding.generation,
11527                PyBytes::new(py, binding.digest.as_bytes()),
11528            ),
11529            meaning,
11530        )
11531            .into_pyobject(py)?
11532            .unbind())
11533    }
11534
11535    /// Return the retained task's checked dependency graph for this live parent.
11536    ///
11537    /// The result is (parent_identity, task_epoch, nodes, feedback_roots).
11538    /// Each node preserves the imported closed-schema order:
11539    /// (identity, kind, data_parents, control_parents, live_envelopes, target,
11540    /// native_record). A native_record is ("statement" | "support" | "observer",
11541    /// index); target is an optional (replay_batch_row, logical_position).
11542    ///
11543    /// These are the actual dependencies retained after import validation,
11544    /// including native-read roots, not a synthesized allowed-support set.
11545    /// They do not replace device query receipts, current feedback validity,
11546    /// token origin records, or a model operand's actual dependency edges.
11547    fn dependency_lineage(&self, py: Python<'_>) -> PyResult<Py<PyTuple>> {
11548        self.session.borrow(py).require_creator()?;
11549        let session = self.session.borrow(py);
11550        let owner = session.owner()?;
11551        let task_use = self.task_use.borrow(py);
11552        task_use.require_current(&owner)?;
11553        let identity = owner
11554            .published_identity(&*self.lease()?)
11555            .map_err(xlog_err)?;
11556        let parent_identity = (
11557            PyBytes::new(py, identity.instance.as_bytes()),
11558            identity.word,
11559            PyBytes::new(py, identity.logical_digest.as_bytes()),
11560            PyBytes::new(py, identity.state_digest.as_bytes()),
11561        );
11562        Ok((
11563            parent_identity,
11564            task_use.task_epoch,
11565            dependency_lineage_object(py, &task_use.authority.dependencies)?,
11566            PyTuple::new(py, &task_use.authority.feedback_roots)?,
11567        )
11568            .into_pyobject(py)?
11569            .unbind())
11570    }
11571
11572    /// Cold read of the complete original model contribution from this parent's
11573    /// native RuntimeContract. Its producer owns format and numerical validation.
11574    /// Use before reconstruction, never within a resident loop. No current model
11575    /// settings are sampled or substituted.
11576    fn model_numerical_mode(&self, py: Python<'_>) -> PyResult<Py<PyAny>> {
11577        self.session.borrow(py).require_creator()?;
11578        let session = self.session.borrow(py);
11579        let mut owner = session.owner()?;
11580        self.task_use.borrow(py).require_current(&owner)?;
11581        let bytes = owner
11582            .published_model_numerical_mode(&*self.lease()?)
11583            .map_err(xlog_err)?;
11584        let value = ColdValue::from_canonical_bytes(&bytes)?;
11585        value.python_value(py)
11586    }
11587
11588    /// Original ring slots as a read-only CUDA DLPack capsule U64[32,8], element
11589    /// strides (8,1), without sorting, repacking or rotating by the ring head.
11590    /// Columns: token, logical_position, kind, provenance, valid, committed,
11591    /// recomputed, provenance_record. Consume once; unused slots are not rows.
11592    /// The capsule retains this reader and Session. Final consumer streams must
11593    /// be joined at release; ``consumer_stream`` follows tensor()'s protocol.
11594    #[pyo3(signature = (*, consumer_stream))]
11595    fn source(&self, py: Python<'_>, consumer_stream: &Bound<'_, PyAny>) -> PyResult<Py<PyAny>> {
11596        self.session.borrow(py).require_creator()?;
11597        let mut budget = 128;
11598        let stream = ColdValue::read(consumer_stream, &mut budget, 0)?.unsigned()?;
11599        let session = self.session.borrow(py);
11600        let mut owner = session.owner()?;
11601        self.task_use.borrow(py).require_current(&owner)?;
11602        let tensor = owner
11603            .published_source(&*self.lease()?, stream)
11604            .map_err(xlog_err)?;
11605        crate::dlpack_capsule_from_tensor(
11606            py,
11607            retain_export_owner(tensor, self.session.clone_ref(py), session.owner_thread)?,
11608        )
11609    }

11611    /// Original terminal flag from this acquired parent's private step inputs,
11612    /// as a single-consumer, read-only-by-contract CUDA DLPack capsule U64[1]
11613    /// with element stride 1. Zero means active; one means Drain is required.
11614    /// This is not a host observation or a replacement for native eligibility.
11615    /// Use for cold reconstruction with the same acquired source/model context.
11616    /// The capsule retains its native step owner and Session; retain the imported
11617    /// tensor until final use and join its consumer streams at release.
11618    /// ``consumer_stream`` follows tensor()'s protocol.
11619    #[pyo3(signature = (*, consumer_stream))]
11620    fn terminal_state(
11621        &self,
11622        py: Python<'_>,
11623        consumer_stream: &Bound<'_, PyAny>,
11624    ) -> PyResult<Py<PyAny>> {
11625        self.session.borrow(py).require_creator()?;

11627        let stream = ColdValue::read(consumer_stream, &mut budget, 0)?.unsigned()?;
11628        let session = self.session.borrow(py);
11629        let mut owner = session.owner()?;
11630        self.task_use.borrow(py).require_current(&owner)?;
11631        let tensor = owner
11632            .published_terminal(&*self.lease()?, stream)
11633            .map_err(xlog_err)?;
